headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure if the source-available leak corpus is fed into the research skill, but direct shared-channel evidence is absent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent B is explicitly about system prompt leaks, so it may contain attacker-controlled instruction-like text. Agent A is a research skill with allowlisted egress, but no shared channel or parser details are documented. Because the interaction is plausible yet undocumented, I choose medium rather than low and note the uncertainty.
conditions: IF agent_a ingests agent_b content through copy-paste, files, or another shared channel
IF agent_a treats external text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep agent_b outputs out of agent_a prompts
Use a manual review step before forwarding text
Prefix imported text as untrusted data
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows sensitive data classes touched, and agent_b has no network egress while agent_a is only allowlisted. A leakage path would need an external shared workspace or manual transfer not documented here, so the blast radius appears small and the pathway is not default.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same workspace containing sensitive files
IF agent_a is prompted with contents copied from agent_b that include secrets
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in any shared folder
Run each agent in separate workspaces
requires-engineering: isolate storage with per-agent ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write surfaces, filesystem permissions, or shared mutable resources are documented for either agent. Agent A has allowlisted egress and agent B has none, but that is not a conflicting write capability. With no shared write path shown, a capability conflict is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or API scope

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s leak-oriented corpus could be used as input to agent A, and agent A could then produce research outputs that B or another downstream step treats as authoritative. No verification or provenance controls are documented, so the cascade is plausible in default operator workflows even though the exact pipeline is not proven.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are forwarded into agent_b or another action-taking step
IF downstream consumers do not verify citations or provenance
mitigations: Require source citations on forwarded outputs
Mark agent A output as provisional

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. Agent A touches no data classes and agent B likewise lists none, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess. The other agent is not cited separately because the relevant compliance fields are absent on both sides.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
